quests.conceptTitle: Subject-Verb Agreement: Be Verb with Plural Subjects
quests.faultySentence: The children is playing in the yard.
quests.correctedSentence: The children are playing in the yard.
quests.ruleExplanation: The subject 'children' is plural, so it needs the plural form 'are' instead of the singular 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Look at the subject 'children' — is it one child or more than one?

quests.faultySentence: The news are on at six o'clock every evening.
quests.correctedSentence: The news is on at six o'clock every evening.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'News' looks plural because of the final -s, but it is grammatically singular and takes 'is', not 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Some nouns that end in -s, like 'news', are actually singular. What verb goes with a singular subject?

quests.conceptTitle: Subject-Verb Agreement: Be Verb with Plural Subjects
quests.faultySentence: The instructions for the new app is confusing everyone in the office.
quests.correctedSentence: The instructions for the new app are confusing everyone in the office.
quests.ruleExplanation: The subject is 'instructions', a plural noun, even though 'app' sits closer to the verb. Plural subjects need 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Find the true subject of the sentence — is it 'instructions' or 'app'?

quests.faultySentence: She don't like spicy food.
quests.correctedSentence: She doesn't like spicy food.
quests.ruleExplanation: With third-person singular subjects like 'she', the negative present tense uses 'doesn't', not 'don't'.
quests.nativeTip: Check the subject 'she' — third-person singular subjects pair with which negative auxiliary?

quests.faultySentence: Does your parents know about the schedule change?
quests.correctedSentence: Do your parents know about the schedule change?
quests.ruleExplanation: The subject 'parents' is plural, so the question needs 'Do', not the singular form 'Does'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Parents' is plural — which question auxiliary matches a plural subject in the present simple?

quests.faultySentence: The manager don't usually answer emails after six o'clock.
quests.correctedSentence: The manager doesn't usually answer emails after six o'clock.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The manager' is singular, so the present-tense negative must be 'doesn't' rather than 'don't'.
quests.nativeTip: Identify the subject performing the action, then decide which negative form matches a singular subject.

quests.faultySentence: He have two brothers and a sister.
quests.correctedSentence: He has two brothers and a sister.
quests.ruleExplanation: Third-person singular subjects such as 'he' require 'has', while 'have' is used with I/you/we/they.
quests.nativeTip: With 'he', 'she', or 'it', which form of this verb is correct?

quests.conceptTitle: Subject-Verb Agreement: Have with Plural Subjects
quests.faultySentence: Both of my roommates has a car.
quests.correctedSentence: Both of my roommates have a car.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Both of my roommates' is a plural subject, so the sentence needs 'have', not the singular 'has'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Both' refers to more than one person — what verb form agrees with a plural subject?

quests.faultySentence: This laptop have a problem with the battery.
quests.correctedSentence: This laptop has a problem with the battery.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'This laptop' is a singular subject, so the sentence requires 'has' instead of 'have'.
quests.nativeTip: Check whether the subject 'laptop' is singular or plural before choosing the verb.

quests.faultySentence: My sister work at a hospital downtown.
quests.correctedSentence: My sister works at a hospital downtown.
quests.ruleExplanation: With a singular subject like 'my sister', present-tense verbs take an -s ending: 'works'.
quests.nativeTip: Third-person singular subjects in the present tense usually add which ending to the verb?

quests.conceptTitle: Subject-Verb Agreement: Plural Subject with Prepositional Phrase
quests.faultySentence: The photos on my phone takes up a lot of space.
quests.correctedSentence: The photos on my phone take up a lot of space.
quests.ruleExplanation: The subject is 'photos', a plural noun; the phrase 'on my phone' does not change the verb form, so the sentence needs 'take'.
quests.nativeTip: Ignore the phrase 'on my phone' for a moment — what is the true subject of the sentence?

quests.faultySentence: The bus usually leave from platform two.
quests.correctedSentence: The bus usually leaves from platform two.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The bus' is singular, so the routine action in the present tense needs the -s form, 'leaves'.
quests.nativeTip: Decide whether 'bus' is singular or plural, then match the verb ending.

quests.faultySentence: She walk to work yesterday because her car wouldn't start.
quests.correctedSentence: She walked to work yesterday because her car wouldn't start.
quests.ruleExplanation: Because the action happened yesterday and is finished, the regular verb needs the past-tense ending: 'walked'.
quests.nativeTip: The word 'yesterday' signals a completed past action — what ending do regular verbs take?

quests.faultySentence: I finish my report before the deadline last week.
quests.correctedSentence: I finished my report before the deadline last week.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Last week' places the action in the finished past, so the verb needs the regular past ending, 'finished', not the base or -s form.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase 'last week' tells you when this happened — what past form is needed?

quests.faultySentence: We wait for twenty minutes at the clinic yesterday.
quests.correctedSentence: We waited for twenty minutes at the clinic yesterday.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since the waiting happened yesterday and is complete, the verb must take the past-tense ending: 'waited'.
quests.nativeTip: Look at the time marker 'yesterday' and decide which past form fits.

quests.faultySentence: I go to the bank this morning to open a new account.
quests.correctedSentence: I went to the bank this morning to open a new account.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Go' is irregular in the past tense; the correct form is 'went', not the base form with -ed.
quests.nativeTip: 'This morning' signals a finished action — what is the irregular past form of 'go'?

quests.faultySentence: He buy a new phone last week because his old one broke.
quests.correctedSentence: He bought a new phone last week because his old one broke.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Buy' has an irregular past form, 'bought'; simply adding -ed would be incorrect.
quests.nativeTip: Think of the irregular past form of 'buy' — it doesn't follow the usual -ed pattern.

quests.faultySentence: The company send the wrong invoice to three different clients last month.
quests.correctedSentence: The company sent the wrong invoice to three different clients last month.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Send' changes irregularly to 'sent' in the past tense, matching the completed action described by 'last month'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Last month' shows this already happened — what's the irregular past tense of 'send'?

quests.conceptTitle: Subject-Verb Agreement: There Is / There Are
quests.faultySentence: There is three empty seats near the window.
quests.correctedSentence: There are three empty seats near the window.
quests.ruleExplanation: Because 'three empty seats' is plural, the sentence needs 'there are', not 'there is'.
quests.nativeTip: Count how many seats are being talked about — one or more than one?

quests.faultySentence: Several people was waiting outside the clinic before it opened.
quests.correctedSentence: Several people were waiting outside the clinic before it opened.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'People' is a plural noun even without an -s ending, so the past tense requires 'were' rather than 'was'.
quests.nativeTip: 'People' is already plural in meaning — what past-tense be verb matches a plural subject?

quests.faultySentence: The children's toys was scattered across the living room floor.
quests.correctedSentence: The children's toys were scattered across the living room floor.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Toys' is plural, so the sentence needs the plural past-tense verb 'were' instead of 'was'.
quests.nativeTip: Identify what was scattered — a single toy or several toys?

quests.faultySentence: This printer aren't working properly today.
quests.correctedSentence: This printer isn't working properly today.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'This printer' is singular, so the negative form should be 'isn't', not the plural 'aren't'.
quests.nativeTip: 'This printer' refers to one machine — which negative be form matches a singular subject?

quests.conceptTitle: Subject-Verb Agreement: Negative Auxiliary with Plural Subjects
quests.faultySentence: My parents doesn't agree with the new policy.
quests.correctedSentence: My parents don't agree with the new policy.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'my parents' is plural, the negative present tense needs 'don't', not the singular form 'doesn't'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Parents' is a plural subject — which negative auxiliary agrees with it in the present tense?

quests.conceptTitle: Negative Verb Forms: Be vs Do
quests.faultySentence: The store isn't accept returns without a receipt.
quests.correctedSentence: The store doesn't accept returns without a receipt.
quests.ruleExplanation: Because 'accept' is an action verb, the negative needs the auxiliary 'doesn't', not a form of 'be' like 'isn't'.
quests.nativeTip: The sentence has a main action verb, 'accept' — should the negative use a form of 'be' or a form of 'do'?

quests.conceptTitle: Subject-Verb Agreement: Plural Subject with Prepositional Phrase
quests.faultySentence: The instructions on the box doesn't make sense to me.
quests.correctedSentence: The instructions on the box don't make sense to me.
quests.ruleExplanation: The subject is 'instructions', which is plural, so the sentence needs 'don't' rather than 'doesn't'.
quests.nativeTip: Find the true subject before the prepositional phrase 'on the box' — is it singular or plural?

quests.faultySentence: Neither of the options seem right for this budget.
quests.correctedSentence: Neither of the options seems right for this budget.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Neither' is grammatically singular, even though it refers to two options, so the verb should be 'seems'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Neither' treats the two options as a single unit — what verb form does that require?

quests.faultySentence: Our internet connection have a problem again this week.
quests.correctedSentence: Our internet connection has a problem again this week.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Connection' is singular, so it takes 'has' rather than 'have'.
quests.nativeTip: Decide if 'connection' is singular or plural before choosing the verb.

quests.faultySentence: Each of the students bring their own laptop to class.
quests.correctedSentence: Each of the students brings their own laptop to class.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Each' is singular, so despite the phrase 'of the students', the verb must be 'brings'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Each' makes the subject singular, even though it's followed by a plural noun — what verb form fits?

quests.conceptTitle: Subject-Verb Agreement: Singular Subject with Plural Modifier
quests.faultySentence: The price of these tickets are higher than I expected.
quests.correctedSentence: The price of these tickets is higher than I expected.
quests.ruleExplanation: The subject is 'price', which is singular; 'of these tickets' only describes it and doesn't change the verb to plural.
quests.nativeTip: Look past 'of these tickets' — what is the actual subject of the sentence?

quests.conceptTitle: Subject-Verb Agreement: One of + Plural Noun
quests.faultySentence: One of my coworkers always arrive late to the Monday meeting.
quests.correctedSentence: One of my coworkers always arrives late to the Monday meeting.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'One of my coworkers' has 'one' as its true subject, which is singular, so the verb needs the -s form 'arrives'.
quests.nativeTip: 'One' is the real subject here — is it singular or plural?
